name: Son Cubano
notes: Son Cubano style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). SALSA'S ANCESTOR, taught as such — a direct cross-link to this app's salsa pack: the clave you learned there was born here. Lineage told straight: son grew in eastern Cuba (Oriente) in the late 1800s from Bantu-Congolese percussion and call-and-response meeting the Spanish tres and décima — an Afro-Cuban creation; the 1920s septets (Ignacio Piñeiro's Septeto Nacional, Trío Matamoros) codified the sound, and the Buena Vista Social Club moment (1997) carried the elders to the world. Design truths: son is danced A CONTRATIEMPO — on the offbeat — which is the pack's central ear-training project and its great gift to any dancer's musicality; the basic is small, elegant and unhurried (son is a conversation, not a workout); partner work is flagged 🤝 late with frame prep solo, in the salsa pack's proven pattern. The clave patterns already in this app's Rhythm Trainer are this pack's home rhythms.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping son clave through one full track — then clap it against the 2-3. The key of the music, owned.
Film yourself stepping ON the offbeat through a slow son — the ear-flip that changes everything.
Film the son basic — small, elegant, a contratiempo — through one full song without drifting onto the beat.
Film the basic with pauses, floreos and your own sabor — dancing the song, not the count.
Take son to a floor — a Cuban night, a salsa social's son set, a casino rueda's slow songs. Your salsa pack and this one now hold hands.

attributes.name: Contratiempo ear L2
attributes.test: clap only the offbeats (the 'and's) through one full son track without collapsing onto the beat

attributes.name: Elegant transfer L1
attributes.test: 20 small weight transfers, full and unhurried, upper body calm as a conversation

nodes.name: The clave — born here
checkpoints: son clave (3-2 and 2-3) is the skeleton key of Afro-Cuban music — and it was forged in son; salsa inherited it from this music
both patterns live in this app's Rhythm Trainer (the salsa pack made you clap them; son makes you understand them)
the bongó's martillo and the tres's guajeo lock around the clave — pick each out by ear

nodes.name: A contratiempo — the offbeat is home
checkpoints: traditional son steps on the OFFBEAT (a contratiempo) — where salsa On1 steps on the beat, son floats between them
hear the difference: march a track on the beat, then step the and's — the second one is son's world
this single ear-skill deepens every dance you own; it's the pack's real payload

nodes.name: Oriente — an Afro-Cuban creation
checkpoints: son grew in eastern Cuba (Oriente) in the late 1800s: Bantu-Congolese percussion and call-and-response meeting the Spanish tres and décima — an Afro-Cuban creation, credited as such
it moved to Havana, and the 1920s septets — Ignacio Piñeiro's Septeto Nacional, Trío Matamoros — codified the golden sound
'Échale Salsita' (Piñeiro, 1933) even seeded the word 'salsa' — the ancestry runs through the vocabulary itself

nodes.name: Salsa's ancestor — the family tree
checkpoints: son → mambo → New York salsa: the trunk this app's salsa pack grows from — two packs, one family
casino (Cuban salsa) and rueda carry son's DNA on Cuban floors today
the Buena Vista Social Club moment (1997) brought the elders — Compay Segundo, Ibrahim Ferrer, Omara Portuondo — to the world; watch them and hear where everything came from

nodes.name: The son basic (a contratiempo)
nodes.anchor: small, elegant, unhurried — a conversation, not a workout
checkpoints: quick-quick-slow stepping on the offbeats — back-replace-pause, forward-replace-pause, compact as a whisper
the pause carries weight: settle into it, don't wait through it
steps small and grounded; elegance is son's athletic feat
if you drift onto the beat, stop, find the and's again, resume — the drift is the lesson
mistakes: dancing salsa On1 timing to son music (the whole point is the flip)
big traveling steps (son barely moves; it deepens instead)

nodes.name: Side basic & the paseo
checkpoints: the same contratiempo phrase traveling side to side, then strolling a small circle (the paseo)
hips settle Cuban-motion soft — the salsa pack's floor-driven motion, slowed to son's temperature
the upper body converses: slight turns, presence, calm

nodes.name: Sabor — pauses & floreos
checkpoints: sabor is flavor: a held pause on the montuno's entrance, a foot floreo, a shoulder's comment on the tres
less, placed exactly, is the whole aesthetic — the elders dance three moves per song and win
improvise within the basic: the phrase is your home, sabor is how you furnish it

nodes.name: Frame & connection prep (solo)
checkpoints: son's hold is close and calm — tall easy posture, arms carrying their own weight
the basic with a light wall-touch: connection without gripping, exactly as the salsa pack drilled
your contratiempo is the gift you bring a partner — a lead or follow who truly hears the and's

nodes.name: The son hold (with a partner)
checkpoints: learned at Cuban nights, casino classes, and salsa socials' son sets — the scene shares floors with salsa everywhere
the couple breathes the pause together; that shared settle is son partnering's whole secret
your salsa partnering (when you get there) and this hold reinforce each other — one family, remember

nodes.name: One son, inhabited — filmed
checkpoints: one classic son (a septet recording or Buena Vista track): basic a contratiempo throughout, paseo once, sabor where the song asks
watch it back listening for the and's — did your feet stay in son's world?
elegance check: could this dance fit in a crowded Havana courtyard? It should

nodes.name: The Cuban night
checkpoints: find son live or social: Cuban music nights, casino rueda communities, the son sets salsa DJs slip in
dance small, listen big; ask an elder to show you one thing
you now dance the root and the branch — salsa and son, one tree

teachers.name: Buena Vista Social Club — the elders, heard
